newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures finish quiet session mixed.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures finish quiet session mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures settled mixed in quiet trading, consolidating after recent steep moves.

December sterling finished moderately lower in a retreat from the contract high set on Tuesday. Sterling posted an inside day on daily bar charts, a typical technical sign that a market is pausing after a steep move, traders said.

December marks and Swiss francs eked out small gains in a rebound from their drop to fresh contract lows Tuesday and again overnight. December yen settled in lower territory, but was up from its overnight contract low, as well.
"There just wasn't much to go on and there weren't any aggressive buyers in the dollar," an IMM trader said.
Several traders noted a flurry of business in yen options late in the day, with the Dec $0.009000/$0.009200 strangle trading about 1,500 times, they said.

Trading was quiet in the contracts that set contract highs and lows on Tuesday, but volume was brisk in Mexican peso futures. The Chicago Mercantile Exhcange estimated Wednesday's overall peso volume at 11,072 contracts.
"It was a big day in the Mexican peso," another IMM trader said. "Peso continues to be the star currency in here."
December peso dropped to the lowest price since early September.
"I think the fact that the peso was down for the fourth consecutive session had people bailing out," a trader said. Traders noted speculative selling and technical deterioration in the market.
Sterling was underpinned early by a UK employment report that showed September unemployment fell 35,600 to a rate of 7.4 percent. That drop was larger than expected, traders and analysts said.
U.S. September consumer prices rose 0.3 percent.

"September CPI data had no impact on trading as the number was precisely on expectations," said Tom O'Malley, senior forex analyst with Thomson Research. "Also, the Bank of Canada rate cut had no net effet on the Canadian dollar," he said.

December yen settled down $0.000005 at $0.008982, marks were up $0.0007 to $0.6523, Swiss francs closed up $0.0005 to $0.7939, and sterling slipped $0.0046 to $1.5830. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
